title: Director at Semiconductor Manufacturer Sees Continued Growth in Marvell Switch and ASIC Activity Despite Capacity Constraints
expert: Director, advanced packaging at ASE (Marvell switch/ASIC development partner; ~30% of workload)
verdict: ASE's packaging director sees Marvell switch/ASIC activity up approximately 50% y/y in Aug–Oct 2026, but available capacity is only about 60% of expected and development lead times are up about 40% vs 90 days ago.

Custom program roster and scope: activity approximately 50% higher y/y (Aug–Oct 2026), first-hand; above BlueFin's MRVL TSMC production +36% y/y for Sept-Q (SB #62115). → Tenet 1 (custom multi-customer) ↑
approximately 30% y/y expected Nov 2026–Jan 2027 (estimate), a slowdown from ~50% and below BlueFin's >40% y/y Dec-Q (SB #62115).
Interconnect growth rate: Broadcom–Marvell Ethernet-switch gap not narrowed in 90 days, first read; projects move from 100T/200T toward 400T next year. → Tenet 3 (scale-up switching) →
Margins: observed product prices approximately 20%–25% higher y/y, first-hand; passes through substrate and node cost; first read on pricing. → Tenet 4 (GM vs opex leverage) ↑
Supply & lead times: capacity about 60% of expected; development lead times up about 40% vs 90 days ago (first-hand); same direction as the distributor call of 2026-11-05 (lead times doubled to 12-24 weeks).
60%–70% confidence the next 3–6 month pipeline lands on schedule (estimate); substrates are the main bottleneck. → Tenet 5 (bear flank) ↑

changes: Activity approximately 50% higher y/y in Aug–Oct 2026 (expert, first-hand) vs BlueFin MRVL TSMC production +36% y/y Sept-Q (SB #62115): consistent, stronger.
Forecast approximately 30% y/y for Nov 2026–Jan 2027 (estimate) vs BlueFin Dec-Q >40% y/y (SB #62115): conflicting (lower).
Development lead times up about 40% vs 90 days ago and capacity at about 60% of expected (expert) vs distributor call 2026-11-05 lead times doubled to 12-24 weeks: consistent (tightening).
Almost all customers negotiating capacity reservations (expert) vs Marvell making capacity payments to reserve supply (SB #60598): consistent.
thesis_impact: Tenet 1 (custom multi-customer): ↑ — Marvell switch/ASIC activity approximately 50% y/y at ASE, new cloud and data-center projects.
Tenet 3 (scale-up switching greenfield): → — Broadcom still leads Ethernet switching; gap not narrowed in 90 days, though projects move to 400T next year.
Tenet 4 (opex leverage > GM dilution): ↑ — observed prices approximately 20%–25% higher y/y pass through rising substrate and node costs.
Tenet 5 (bear flank): ↑ — capacity about 60% of expected and only 60%–70% schedule confidence put timing risk on the ramp.
